metaDescription: Odoo Maintenance implementation detail: preventive requests that keep firing, MTBF and MTTR you can defend, spare parts, and what the app will not do.
intro: Odoo Maintenance is a Community app, so it adds no licence cost on either edition. You get an equipment register, maintenance teams, corrective and preventive requests on a kanban board, and computed MTBF, MTTR and an estimated next failure per machine. What you do not get is a stock move for spare parts, a cost field on the request, or a running hours meter.

Maintenance projects fail at the register, not at the software. Four hundred imported rows of Compressor 3, with no category, no location and no technician, produce a board nobody opens. Categories set the responsible user and the team. The preventive frequency drives the request generator. The stage flagged as done drives every reliability figure the reporting screens will show you.
whoFor: Manufacturers running MRP work centres, where a stopped machine holds up a work order.
Facilities teams with a fixed base of chillers, lifts, generators and pumps serviced on a calendar.
Plants, hospitals and laboratories that must show an auditor a dated inspection record per asset.
Not for companies selling maintenance to customers, since a request has no customer, price or contract.
Not for a single site with twenty assets and a spreadsheet that already works.

capabilities.title: The equipment register
capabilities.body: Each asset carries a category, a maintenance team, a technician, a location and either a department or an employee it is assigned to, plus vendor, model, serial number, effective date, purchase cost and warranty expiry. The category is not a label. It sets the default responsible user and team, and it is what every report groups by, so a thin category tree costs you later.

capabilities.title: Preventive requests that generate themselves
capabilities.body: Set a preventive frequency in days and an expected duration on the equipment. Odoo derives a next action date from the last completed preventive request, and a daily scheduled action creates the request when that date arrives, with the team and technician copied from the equipment record. Closing it in a stage flagged as done is what rolls the date forward for the next cycle.

capabilities.title: Corrective requests, MTBF and MTTR
capabilities.body: A breakdown is a corrective request with a priority, a blocked or ready state and a scheduled date. From closed corrective requests Odoo computes mean time between failure, mean time to repair, the latest failure date and an estimated next failure per machine. You can also enter an expected MTBF by hand and compare the target against the measured figure, which is the first number a plant manager asks for.

capabilities.title: The manufacturing work centre link
capabilities.body: The standard bridge puts equipment on a work centre. An operator blocks that centre from the work order, which raises a corrective request and changes the working state of the centre, so planning stops offering capacity that does not exist. Closing the request releases it. This is the one integration that changes behaviour rather than adding another screen to look at.

capabilities.title: Teams, reporting and intake
capabilities.body: Requests belong to a team and render as kanban, list, calendar on the scheduled date, pivot and graph, all in Community. An equipment category can be given an incoming mail alias, so a message from a site lands as a request on the right team. On Enterprise every operator who types a request needs a user licence, which is why intake often runs through that alias.

setup.title: Design the category tree first
setup.body: Categories drive the default responsible user, the team that picks the work up and every grouping in reporting. Eight to fifteen categories by asset type, such as compressors, HVAC, forklifts and production lines, works better than a tree copying the org chart or the site plan. Location, department and team are separate fields, so keep them out of the category name.

setup.title: Import the register with the automation fields filled
setup.body: A register carrying only name and category leaves the app inert. Load serial number, location, effective date, technician, team, warranty expiry and the preventive frequency in the same file. A blank frequency means no preventive request is ever generated for that asset, and an import that skipped that column is the usual reason a go live produces an empty board.

setup.title: Fix the stage model and the done flag
setup.body: Default stages are New Request, In Progress, Repaired and Scrap. Only a stage flagged as done writes the close date, and that date is what MTTR and the next preventive date are computed from. Add a waiting on parts stage if that state is real, keep the done flag on closing stages only, and train the team that moving the card is the record.

setup.title: Decide how spare parts leave stock, on day one
setup.body: Odoo will not move stock from a maintenance request. Choose the method before go live: an internal transfer to a maintenance location, a scrap against the machine, or a purchase delivered direct to the job. Set an analytic account per equipment or per category as well, so parts and contractor bills land somewhere you can report on per asset, month by month.

pitfalls.title: Spare parts end up in a text field
pitfalls.body: With no agreed method technicians type part numbers into the description, because there is no stock move behind a maintenance request. Six months on the figures for filters, seals and bearings are wrong, nobody trusts reordering, and cost per machine cannot be produced. This is fixed in configuration with a transfer or a scrap step, never by a report afterwards.

pitfalls.title: The preventive schedule stops without telling anyone
pitfalls.body: The next action date comes from the last completed preventive request. Leave one request sitting in progress and the clock for that asset stops quietly, while the board still looks busy. Build a filter on equipment whose next action date has already passed and review it weekly. This behaviour is what turns a rollout into a complaint by month three.

pitfalls.title: Running hours and odometers are not in the app
pitfalls.body: The preventive frequency is calendar days. There is no meter reading on the equipment record, so a rule such as service every 250 running hours is not standard behaviour. The numbers usually exist elsewhere, an odometer log in Fleet or work order durations in Manufacturing, and turning either into a trigger is a custom build. Scope it as a build.

pitfalls.title: Reliability figures nobody believes
pitfalls.body: MTBF and MTTR inherit the habits of whoever raises the requests. Three requests for one breakdown, a failure logged two days late, or a dead machine archived instead of scrapped, and the mean time between failure on screen is fiction. Agree one request per failure event, and a rule that a failure is logged in the shift it happened, before any of these numbers reach management or a customer contract review.

pitfalls.title: Fleet and Maintenance are two registers
pitfalls.body: Vehicles in Odoo Fleet keep their own service and repair logs and are not maintenance equipment records. No standard bridge joins the two, so a workshop servicing both plant and vehicles ends up with two histories and two definitions of overdue. Decide which register owns each asset class at the start, and build a link only where reporting needs one.

worksWith: Manufacturing, for equipment on work centres and blocking a centre while a request is open
Inventory, for the spare parts location and the transfer or scrap behind each job
Purchase and Accounting, for contractor bills and the analytic distribution that builds cost per asset
Fleet, which keeps its own vehicle service log and needs an ownership decision per asset class
Employees, for equipment assigned to a person or a department and for the technician list
Field Service on Enterprise, where the same crew also does billable work at customer sites

regional.note: Maintenance under an annual contract is a standard tax invoice, so under ZATCA Phase 2 it clears Fatoora before it is valid and a signed job sheet is not a bill. Invoice fields carry Arabic. A site team on your own payroll is paid through the wage protection system.

The Electronic Invoicing System routes documents through an Accredited Service Provider, the largest businesses from 1 January 2027 and the rest from 1 July 2027. A contract billed monthly is a continuous supply, so the tax point follows the invoice or the payment. Technician pay runs through WPS and gratuity accrues per employee.

One maintenance invoice can touch two authorities. The service is provincial sales tax, so SRB in Sindh, PRA in Punjab, KPRA or BRA elsewhere, while the spare part fitted is federal sales tax to the FBR. FBR digital invoicing clears first, so the invoice number and QR code come back from PRAL or a licensed integrator.

Maintenance sits in the SAC 9987 service group and is taxed differently to the part fitted, so one invoice carries a service code and a goods code. Equipment sent to a workshop and back moves on a delivery challan with an e-way bill above the state threshold, and above the turnover limit the invoice needs an IRN.

Periodic control of work equipment, lifting gear and pressure vessels by an authorised person is a standing obligation, and the certificate belongs on the equipment record rather than in a drawer. Parts dispatched to site need an e-Irsaliye. Billing splits between e-Fatura and e-Arsiv by counterparty, and records stay hosted in Turkiye.

Lifting equipment needs a thorough examination under LOLER, every six months where it lifts people and every twelve months otherwise, while PUWER covers the rest of the plant. Those intervals are what the preventive frequency should be set from. VAT on the billing side is filed under Making Tax Digital, and repairs to structures can fall inside CIS.

BetrSichV requires a written risk assessment that sets the inspection interval for each item of work equipment, and DGUV Vorschrift 3 sets the electrical testing cycle, so the frequency on the record has to match the assessment rather than a supplier leaflet. Records feeding an invoice fall under GoBD, and the ledger exports to DATEV.

faqs.q: Is Odoo Maintenance in Community, or does it need Enterprise?
faqs.a: The Maintenance app is Community, included on both editions at no extra licence cost. What is Enterprise is most of what people want around it: Field Service for billable work at customer sites, Studio for extra fields such as a meter reading, IoT, and the Odoo mobile app. Maintenance alone does not force an edition change.

faqs.q: Can Odoo trigger preventive maintenance on running hours or kilometres?
faqs.a: Not as standard. The preventive frequency is in days and there is no meter field to compare a reading against. Fleet keeps an odometer log for vehicles and Manufacturing records work order durations, so the data usually exists. Turning either into a trigger that creates a request is a custom automation and should be priced as one.

faqs.q: Does a maintenance request take spare parts out of stock?
faqs.a: No. There is no stock move behind a maintenance request. Parts are handled beside it: an internal transfer to a maintenance location, a scrap against the machine, or a purchase delivered direct. If consumption has to post from the request itself, that is a development, and it is the most common first extension.

faqs.q: How does Odoo calculate MTBF and MTTR?
faqs.a: Both come from corrective requests on the equipment. Mean time between failure uses the intervals between failures, mean time to repair uses the time from request to close date, and the close date is written only when the request reaches a stage flagged as done. An expected MTBF can be entered by hand for comparison.

faqs.q: Can we invoice a customer for maintenance from this app?
faqs.a: No. Requests carry no customer, no price and no link to a sale order. Selling maintenance means Sales for the contract, Subscriptions for a recurring fee and Field Service on Enterprise for the visit that gets billed. The Maintenance app is for your own assets, and mixing the two in one register is why a rebuild follows.

faqs.q: What actually takes the time on a maintenance implementation?
faqs.a: The register. Configuring categories, teams, stages and preventive rules is short work. Collecting serial numbers, locations, warranty dates and a defensible service interval for every asset, then getting technicians to log work on the day it happens, is what decides whether the reliability numbers are worth reading.
